text:
jordan: heads up — seeing recurring small-write latency spikes in eu-south2 nightly window (02:00-03:30 UTC) for the last 4 days. GPU attach waits ~2-3m in that window, some jobs fell back to Dedicated. anyone tracking a compaction/cleanup job?
ops-bot: ALERT: iops_spike detected eu-south2 cluster-scratchpool average_io_wait 37ms at 2024-10-12T02:05Z (auto-alert threshold 20ms) :warning:
anika: I grabbed the perf traces and it lines up with our metadata compaction job starting. prefix KV sweeps + smallwrite stream = lots of tiny random IO. p99 write latency jumps from ~4ms -> ~60ms.
matt: do we have which gnodes/pools are hit? is this concentrated or fleet-wide?
jordan: mainly scratchpool-gnode cohorts 7/8/9, but the compaction is a job spread over many gn(s). sample logs: ```Oct 12 02:05:02 gnode-08 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme1n1, sector 12345678
2024-10-12T02:05:03 scratch-cleaner[2145]: compaction: kv-prefix sweep start shard=7
2024-10-12T02:07:12 gpu-scheduler[pid]: attach_wait 128s pod=ml-train-43
```
clare: that blk_update_request looks scary but it's correlated with IO saturation not raw device failure (SMART ok). Could be write-amplification + thermal hysteresis.
anika: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) throttle compaction concurrency (reduce compaction workers to 1 per gnode) 2) ionice/blkprio compaction process to low IO priority so scheduler attach wins.
matt: +1 to throttle. also can we shift compaction window to 05:00-06:30 UTC in eu-south2 for a week and monitor?
jordan: we should avoid shifting globally — region has peak TPU usage earlier. propose: throttled compaction + testing ionice on a small canary set (gnode-08). If stable, roll to other gnodes and then consider window shift.
clare: here's a quick systemd drop-in we can test on the compaction runner to lower IO priority: ```[Unit]
Description=KV compactor (drop-in throttled)
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/kv-compactor --shard=%i
CPUWeight=10
IOSchedulingClass=2
IOSchedulingPriority=7
``` apply via: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kv-compactor@7`
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduling change triggered maintenance window 2024-10-12T03:10Z (automated).
anika: also looking at scratchpool quotas — we can bump smallwrite coalescing in the kernel module we maintain (experiment flag) which reduced tinywrites by ~30% in staging. Patch to flip on for canary: ```sysctl -w fs.scratch.coalesce_small_writes=1```
matt: what's the cost tradeoff? coalescing increases memory for buffering; could push up swap usage on smaller GNODES. Need canary + OOM guard.
jordan: plan: 1) enable systemd IO lowering on gnode-08 compactor tonight 2) throttle compactor workers from 4->1 across shard 7 3) enable coalesce sysctl on gnode-08 canary 4) monitor GPU attach p99 and io_wait for 48h — if good, roll to shard 8/9. I'll open the rollout PR and link the k8s job patch.
clare: :+1: please tag me on the PR, I can help with the canary runbook and rollback steps.
anika: i'll wire alerts to suppress noisy Dedicated-fallback signals while we test (we don't want pager spam).
matt: also ping firmware vendor if blk_update_request reappears after mitigation — might be controller queue starvation.
jordan: ack. I'll create a short postmortem draft if we see >1h of degraded attach. For now executing canary at 02:30 UTC.
ops-bot: REMINDER: gpu-allocations monitoring: p99_attach_wait metric emitted (team:eng-infra) — 02:45 UTC baseline capture started. :eyes:
